items.text: Public members that are not XNA 4.0 API carry the EXT suffix but no CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them: Texture::GetFormatSizeEXT, Texture::GetBlockSizeSquaredEXT, GameWindow::getIsBorderlessEXTProperty and setIsBorderlessEXTProperty. CHECKLIST.md requires every member outside the XNA 4.0 surface to be marked.
items.evidence: modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture.hpp (public static GetBlockSizeSquaredEXT, GetFormatSizeEXT, unmarked); modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GameWindow.hpp (public getIsBorderlessEXTProperty/setIsBorderlessEXTProperty, unmarked); CHECKLIST.md (CNAEXT markers)

items.text: The strict XNA-purity compile check (cna_strict_xna_api_check and its WILL_FAIL leak twin) exercises only the Microsoft::Devices/Sensors surface; no automated check covers marker completeness or strict-mode purity of the graphics, content, input, audio or media surfaces.

Documentation lag in CNA's own README: it calls CNA_STRICT_XNA_API 'a dedicated CMake build option' (no CMake option declares it), prints the pre-closure 3,467/3,627 member figure and '0/31' oracle scenes, and says CNA is 'built on SDL3'.
items.evidence: README.md (Project Status, Verification methodology); CMake declares no CNA_STRICT_XNA_API option; docs/xna-4-runtime-member-coverage.md (3,627/3,627)

items.section: The CNAEXT tag: a compiler-enforced honesty check
items.text: Stale paths in CNA documents: CNAHelper.hpp's comment names tests/Microsoft/Devices/StrictXnaApiSurfaceCheck.cpp (the file is tools/devices/); THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md places the vendored Stock Effects HLSL under src/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D9/shaders/xna/ (now modules/renderers/directx9/src/shaders/xna/).

items.section: Interfaces as abstract base classes, IDisposable as a pattern
items.text: CLAUDE.md's IDisposable rule says to throw std::runtime_error on use after disposal, and its Behavior Fidelity list names std::out_of_range/std::runtime_error, while XNA-layer code throws System::ObjectDisposedException and System::ArgumentOutOfRangeException; the written rule lags the code.

items.section: Glossary of XNA and CNA Terms
items.text: The glossary states that GraphicsCapability MRT and occlusion-query false positives are confirmed. At TARGET the base IGraphicsRenderer::SupportsCapability default is still permissive for the original members and DIRECTX9 inherits it wholesale, but DIRECTX9 implements MRT (bounded by NumSimultaneousRTs) and occlusion queries; which renderer, if any, still reports a false positive was not re-established.

items.section: Glossary of XNA and CNA Terms
items.text: DIRECTX12 descriptor heaps described as fixed-capacity bump allocators with no slot reclamation during a device lifetime, making descriptor exhaustion a CNA limit.
items.evidence: modules/renderers/directx12/src/D3D12DescriptorHeaps.cpp (AppendBlock doubles capacity; ReclaimCompleted recycles fence-completed descriptors)

items.section: Glossary of XNA and CNA Terms
items.text: sharp-runtime MemoryStream's raw-buffer constructor described as creating a read-only stream where .NET defaults to writable (a known divergence).
items.evidence: sharp-runtime@41b918c9 modules/io/include/System/IO/MemoryStream.hpp (MemoryStream(const bytecs*, intcs, bool writable = true))

items.section: Glossary of XNA and CNA Terms
items.text: HEADLESS described as reporting the last Clear() colour; its back-buffer readback formerly filled the caller's buffer with that colour, indistinguishable from a real frame.
Morph targets described as POSITION/NORMAL only with tangent deltas out of scope.
The doc comment of BlendMorphTargetsEXT says attributes other than Position/Normal are copied unchanged, but the implementation also blends tangent directions; comment lags code.

The experimental C API release gate reports 'Not ready'. At TARGET the single unmet criterion is 'No public C++ symbol is unaccounted for' (468 public symbols unmapped), not unclassified modules as the preface says; no CI job builds the C library.

items.section: xna4-spec: a ground truth to audit against
items.text: xna4-spec's README says its index covers 550 types while index.xml and the tree hold 544 type files; sibling documentation drift, and CNA does not use xna4-spec.

items.section: Missing dependencies: stub correctly, never invent
items.text: BinaryReader::ReadChar() was described as throwing FormatException for a code point above 0xFFFF; sharp-runtime now returns a surrogate pair across two reads.
